title: Pulsed field ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation with atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia under tubeless general anesthesia: a case report.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) combined with left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has long been used in the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is now increasingly adopted due to its great precision and improved safety profile. This report presents a rare case of PFA performed for persistent AF and atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT), along with LAAC, under non-intubated general anesthesia.

CASE DESCRIPTION: A 36-year-old male patient presented with a 10-year history of recurrent chest tightness and palpitations, which had worsened during the week prior to admission. He was diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy and AF 4 months ago and had a previous cerebral infarction, with a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 3 and a HAS-BLED score of 1. A one-stop procedure combining PFA and LAAC was planned. During ablation at the roof of the right superior pulmonary vein, AF converted to sinus rhythm and subsequently developed spontaneous tachycardia, suspected to be AVRT due to a left-sided accessory pathway near CS1-2. Therefore, ablation of the accessory pathway and mitral isthmus was performed, and atrioventricular separation and mitral isthmus block were confirmed. A total of 78 discharges were delivered throughout the procedure, and repeated high-frequency atrial stimulation did not induce atrial flutter or AF. LAAC was then completed as planned. Electrocardiogram (ECG) showed sinus rhythm, and echocardiography demonstrated improved cardiac remodeling at 3-month follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: AVRT is a type of supraventricular tachycardia caused by the presence of an accessory pathway due to congenital structural abnormalities. Our case reports an AVRT occurrence during PFA for AF and provides significant evidence that PFA is effective and safe for accessory pathway ablation during AF ablation.

title: A predictive model for heart failure in patients with hypertension and persistent atrial fibrillation: A retrospective single-center study.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate a predictive nomogram for heart failure in patients with hypertension and persistent atrial fibrillation (HT-PeAF).

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed clinical data from patients with HT-PeAF hospitalized at Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital between 2010 and 2019. Predictive variables were selected based on multivariable logistic regression analysis and clinical relevance, which were then incorporated into a clinical nomogram. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for discrimination, the Hosmer-Lemeshow test for calibration, and decision curve analysis for clinical utility.

RESULTS: Of the 395 enrolled patients, 151 experienced heart failure. Nine predictive variables were identified: prior catheter ablation, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, hemoglobin, uric acid, creatinine, total bilirubin, fasting blood glucose, red blood cell distribution width, and coronary artery disease. The nomogram demonstrated good discriminative ability (AUC = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.72-0.81), good calibration (P = 0.44), and favorable clinical utility.

CONCLUSION: This accessible tool facilitates individualized risk stratification for heart failure in HT-PeAF patients, though prospective validation in multicenter Asian cohorts is warranted.

title: Association of Iron Homeostasis With One-Year All-Cause Mortality Among Intensive Care Unit Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: A Retrospective Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Perturbations in iron homeostasis can substantially affect cardiovascular outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the prognostic value of various iron homeostasis indicators for all-cause mortality in critically ill AF patients.

METHOD: Data for this retrospective study were obtained from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database. Based on the iron homeostasis-related indicators (ferritin, serum iron, transferrin, and total iron-binding capacity [TIBC]), the risks of 1-year mortality among critically ill patients with atrial fibrillation were calculated using Cox proportional-hazards regression. Associations of iron homeostasis indicators with all-cause mortality in critically ill AF patients were assessed via Kaplan-Meier curves, restricted cubic splines, and subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: After multivariable adjustment, patients in the highest ferritin quartile had a greater risk of 1-year mortality than those in the lowest quartile (Q4 HR 1.277, 95% CI 1.083-1.506, p < 0.01). In contrast, the highest quartiles of transferrin (Q4 HR 0.732, 95% CI 0.622-0.861, p < 0.01) and TIBC (Q4 HR 0.732, 95% CI 0.622-0.861, p < 0.01) were associated with lower mortality. No significant association was observed between serum iron quartiles and 1-year mortality (Q4 HR 1.067, 95% CI 0.914-1.245, p = 0.41). Restricted cubic spline analyses further characterized the exposure and outcome patterns for these iron-related parameters.

CONCLUSION: Among critically ill patients with AF, ferritin, transferrin and TIBC levels were independently associated with 1-year all-cause mortality. No significant association was observed for serum iron.

title: Association Between Left Atrial Volume Index (LAVI) and Glycemic Control (HbA1c) in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Glycemic control and left atrial remodeling in patients with concomitant type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unclear. In this study, we examined the association between glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and left atrial volume index (LAVI) in this high-risk population.

METHODS: A total of 700 patients with AF and T2DM were included in this retrospective study. We used medical records to obtain HbA1c and echocardiographic parameters. We assessed LAVI as a continuous variable and as a binary variable (enlarged LAVI > 34 mL/m²). We used Spearman correlation, multivariable linear regression, and binary logistic regression to examine the relationship between HbA1c and LAVI.

RESULTS: There was a significant association between higher HbA1c and greater LAVI (Spearman's ρ = 0.287, p < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, each 1% increase in HbA1c was associated with a 1.678 mL/m² increase in LAVI. Higher HbA1c was independently associated with increased odds of enlarged LAVI (adjusted odds ratio (OR) = 1.701, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.391-2.081, p < 0.001). Hypertension, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease were also independently associated with enlarged LAVI.

CONCLUSION: In patients with concurrent AF and T2DM, higher HbA1c was independently associated with larger LAVI and higher odds of left atrial enlargement (LAE). Future prospective studies are warranted to determine whether improved glycemic control can influence atrial remodeling.

title: Oral Obesity Medicines in the Era of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome (CKM): Beyond Weight Loss Toward Disease Modification.
summary: Obesity is a major driver of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome and contributes to the development of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes. Historically, oral obesity pharmacotherapy was evaluated primarily according to weight loss efficacy. However, the emergence of the CKM framework has shifted therapeutic priorities toward modifying obesity related complications and improving long term clinical outcomes. This review summarizes currently approved oral obesity medications, including first generation agents (orlistat, phentermine/topiramate, and naltrexone/bupropion) and second generation incretin-based therapies (oral semaglutide and orforglipron), within the context of CKM syndrome. First generation agents provide modest-to-moderate weight loss and variable metabolic benefits, but evidence supporting cardiovascular or kidney outcome improvement remains limited and largely observational. In contrast, oral incretin-based therapies demonstrate broader effects across the CKM spectrum, including substantial weight reduction, improved glycemic control, favorable effects on blood pressure and triglycerides, and emerging kidney benefits. Among currently available oral agents, oral semaglutide has the strongest evidence, with the SOUL trial demonstrating a reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events in high-risk individuals with type 2 diabetes. Signals suggesting benefits in heart failure and atrial fibrillation are encouraging but remain exploratory. Orforglipron represents the first non-peptide oral glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist and offers simplified administration with promising metabolic efficacy; however, cardiovascular, kidney, heart failure, and arrhythmia outcome data are still awaited. Collectively, the role of oral obesity pharmacotherapy is evolving from weight management alone toward comprehensive CKM care.

title: From wrist to heart: clinical validation and real-world translation of wearable and portable AI-enhanced electrocardiography.
summary: Wearable and portable electrocardiogram (ECG) devices are shifting cardiovascular monitoring beyond clinician-directed testing, driven by consumer-led self-monitoring, remote care, and preventive cardiology. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enhance the value of these devices by supporting automated interpretation, but clinical translation remains uneven. This narrative review synthesises current evidence on AI-enhanced ECG (AI-ECG) analysis in wearable and portable systems, with emphasis on the gap between technical performance and real-world implementation. Although many advances have been developed using conventional 12-lead ECG datasets, deployment in wearable and portable devices introduces additional challenges related to device-specific signal acquisition, preprocessing, domain shift, and user-led recording. Evidence is most mature for atrial fibrillation detection, while applications across conduction disease, other arrhythmias, structural phenotypes, and prognostic assessment remain earlier in development and are supported by fewer prospective, device-specific evaluations. Across the field, retrospective and dataset-based studies predominate, with limited evidence that improved detection translates into better patient outcomes or health-system efficiency. Future research should evaluate performance using the intended device, population, and clinical pathway, and determine whether AI-ECG changes management without increasing unnecessary investigation or workload. Establishing clinical value, rather than improving classification accuracy alone, will determine the role of wearable and portable AI-ECG in routine cardiovascular care.

title: Pulsed Field Ablation as First-Line Therapy for the Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation: a FARADISE Sub-Analysis.
The Prevalence and Clinical Characteristics of Atrial Fibrillation and Reflux Esophagitis Among Individuals Undergoing Health Checkups.
summary: Objective To examine the association between atrial fibrillation (AF) and reflux esophagitis (RE).Methods A total of 5,205 adults (3,262 men, 1,943 women; mean age, 54.9±9.8 years) who underwent esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) as part of a routine health checkup were enrolled in this study. AF was defined as AF detected on electrocardiography during the checkup and/or a documented history of the condition. RE was assessed endoscopically according to the Los Angeles classification. The smoking history, habitual alcohol consumption, and use of acid-suppressive agents were also assessed.Results AF was observed in 36 participants (0.7%). Compared with those without AF, participants with AF were more likely to be male, older, have a higher body mass index, and have a history of smoking and acid-suppressive agent use. After excluding participants receiving acid-suppressive medications, RE was significantly more prevalent in patients with AF than in those without AF (39.1% vs. 22.0%, p=0.049). The prevalence of AF was 0.9% among patients with RE and 0.4% among those without RE. However, multiple logistic regression analysis indicated that RE was not independently associated with AF after adjusting for sex, age, and other clinical factors.Conclusion AF may be associated with RE in individuals undergoing routine health checkups. However, this association was attenuated after adjustment for sex, age, and other clinical factors, suggesting that it may be largely explained by shared confounding factors.

title: High-Frequency Low-Tidal Volume Ventilation and Procedural Efficiency in Atrial Fibrillation Catheter Ablation: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
summary:
OBJECTIVES: To compare high-frequency low-tidal volume (HFLTV) ventilation with standard ventilation (SV) regarding procedural efficiency, airway mechanics, and clinical outcomes in atrial fibrillation (AF) catheter ablation.

DESIGN: Retrospective, observational, nonrandomized cohort study.

SETTING: Electrophysiology laboratory of a single tertiary-care university hospital.

PARTICIPANTS: There were 160 consecutive eligible adults undergoing first-time AF radiofrequency ablation under general anesthesia between June 2023 and May 2024.

INTERVENTIONS: Patients received HFLTV (n = 80; respiratory rate 25-30 breaths/min, tidal volume 3-4 mL/kg, ETCO₂ maintained <50 mmHg) or SV (n = 80; tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg, respiratory rate 10-12 breaths/min) per attending anesthesiologist practice. All received propofol-remifentanil total intravenous anesthesia.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Primary outcomes were total procedure time and radiofrequency ablation time; secondary outcomes were airway pressures, oxygenation, AF recurrence at 1 and 6 months, AF-related hospitalization, and complications. HFLTV was associated with lower median procedure time (110 v 128 minutes; p < .001) and ablation time (23 v 28 minutes; p < .001). Peak (14 v 18 cmH₂O) and minimum (13 v 15 cmH₂O) airway pressures were lower with HFLTV (both p < .001), whereas ETCO₂ and SpO₂ nadir were comparable. Multivariable regression identified HFLTV as an independent predictor of shorter ablation time (nonstandardized β=-5.48 minutes; 95% CI -7.05 to -3.91; p < .001). In exploratory analyses, recurrence at 1 month (7.5% v 15.0%; p = .211) and 6 months (13.8% v 18.8%; p = .520) and 6-month AF-related hospitalization (12.5% v 18.8%; p = .384) were numerically lower with HFLTV but confidence intervals were wide and included no difference.

CONCLUSION: In a consecutive cohort including paroxysmal and persistent AF, HFLTV was associated with shorter procedure and ablation times and lower measured airway pressures without compromising gas exchange. Clinical outcome analyses were exploratory and hypothesis-generating, warranting prospective randomized evaluation.

title: Temporal dynamics of left atrial reverse remodeling predicts atrial fibrillation ablation outcome: A 3-year longitudinal study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Long-term dynamic changes in the left atrium (LA) following radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) for atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unclear. We aimed to unveil the temporary dynamics of LA reverse remodeling and the optimal echocardiographic indicator and timing for evaluating RFCA outcomes in this 3-year longitudinal study.

METHODS: Data were retrospectively collected from 400 consecutive patients undergoing RFCA for AF (paroxysmal 71%). Echocardiographic examinations were performed at 1 day, and 1, 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, and 36 months after RFCA. Patients were classified into three groups based on RFCA outcomes. We constructed mean response curves to visualize the tendency between echocardiographic indicators and time across groups. Proportional odds models were built to determine the optimal echocardiographic indicator and follow-up time point for distinguishing the outcome group.

RESULTS: After a mean follow-up duration of 81 ± 24 months, free of AF was achieved in 357 patients. Mean response curves of echocardiographic indicators differed between patients with and without AF recurrence. A flat slope of mean response curves in the first 3 months and deterioration of echocardiographic indices starting 18 months after RFCA indicated higher risks of AF recurrence. LA linear ablation didn't affect the longitudinal trend of echocardiographic indicators in paroxysmal AF, but retarded LA reverse remodeling process in persistent AF. LAEF at 36 months had the highest c-index for predicting AF recurrence during a median follow-up period of 80 months.

CONCLUSIONS: The longitudinal trend of echocardiographic indicators reflects long-term LA remodeling and can provide important information for individualized treatment strategies.

title: Pulsed Field Versus Radiofrequency Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation: Esophageal Lesions and Suspected Gastroparesis
summary: Background Esophageal mucosal injury and gastroparesis are clinically important complications of radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) is a non-thermal modality that may spare these complications due to its myocardial tissue selectivity.Objectives We aimed to compare the incidence of endoscopically detected esophageal lesions (EDELs) and suspected gastroparesis between RFA and PFA as the primary endpoints. Secondary endpoints included perioperative complications, procedural parameters, and 365-day clinical outcomes.Methods Between July 2023 and July 2025, patients undergoing a first-time AF ablation with RFA or PFA were enrolled. RFA was performed using either a QDOT MICRO catheter (Biosense Webster, Inc., Irvine, CA, USA) or a TactiFlex Ablation Catheter, Sensor Enabled (Abbott, Abbott Park, IL, USA), while PFA was performed using the FARAPULSE system or the PulseSelect system. All patients underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy on the day after ablation. An EDEL was defined as esophageal erythema, erosion, ulcer, or atrio-esophageal fistula. Suspected gastroparesis was defined as gastric food residue after > 12 h of overnight fasting. Clinical follow-up was performed with 12-lead or Holter electrocardiography.Results A total of 84 patients were included (RFA: n = 43; PFA: n = 41). Esophageal erosion was observed in 2 patients in the RFA group (4.7%) and in none in the PFA group (p = 0.49). Suspected gastroparesis occurred in 15 patients treated with RFA (34.9%) and in none treated with PFA (P<0.001). All patients were asymptomatic during endoscopy. No other procedural complications were observed in either group. The total procedure time was significantly shorter with PFA (158.5 ± 40.8 vs. 193.8 ± 38.3 min, p < 0.001), while the fluoroscopy time was longer. At 365 days, atrial arrhythmia recurrence rates were comparable between the two groups (p = 0.47).Conclusions In this single-center cohort, PFA was associated with a significantly lower incidence of suspected gastroparesis than RFA, and no EDELs were observed in the PFA group. PFA may reduce gastrointestinal injury associated with AF ablation. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and clarify their clinical significance.

title: Open-Irrigated Versus Non-Irrigated Catheters in SVT Ablation: Substrate-Specific Outcomes in AVRT and AVNRT
summary: Background Open-irrigated catheters (OIC) provide improved cooling, deeper lesion formation, and enhanced safety during radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA). However, comparative evidence regarding substrate-specific outcomes with OIC versus non-irrigated catheters (NIC) for supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) remains limited. This study compared acute ablation success (AAS) and recurrence after first-time RFCA using OIC versus NIC, with particular emphasis on differential outcomes in atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia (AVRT) and atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia (AVNRT).Methods A retrospective cohort of consecutive patients undergoing first-time RFCA for AVNRT or AVRT between 2017 and 2023 was analyzed. Patients were categorized by catheter type (OIC vs. NIC). Primary outcomes were AAS and SVT recurrence during 24-month follow-up. Multivariate logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used for adjusted analyses. Subgroup analyses were performed for AVNRT and AVRT.Results Among 302 procedures, OIC were used in 113 (37.4%). Overall AAS was achieved in 85.4% of cases (92.0% OIC vs. 81.5% NIC; p = 0.012). Recurrence occurred in 17.9% (7.1% OIC vs. 24.3% NIC; p < 0.001). In multivariable analyses, OIC use was independently associated with higher AAS (adjusted RR 1.12; 95% CI 1.05-1.20; p = 0.001) and lower recurrence (adjusted HR 0.24; 95% CI 0.12-0.52; p < 0.001). In the AVRT subgroup, OIC use was associated with higher AAS (89.9% vs. 76.6%; p = 0.014) and lower recurrence (adjusted HR 0.25; 95% CI 0.11-0.57; p < 0.001), whereas no significant differences were observed in AVNRT.Conclusions In this cohort, OIC use was associated with higher AAS and lower recurrence, with the favorable association primarily observed in AVRT rather than AVNRT. These findings support further evaluation of substrate-specific catheter selection, particularly for accessory pathway ablation.

title: [Supraventricular tachycardia in advanced age].
Acute lymphocytic myocarditis complicated by bidirectional ventricular tachycardia treated with early steroid use.
summary: Acute lymphocytic myocarditis can precipitate malignant ventricular arrhythmias, including the rare presentation of bidirectional ventricular tachycardia (BDVT), a rhythm associated with significant hemodynamic instability. Although BDVT is classically linked to catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and digitalis toxicity, it is increasingly recognized in myocarditis, likely reflecting diffuse inflammatory involvement of the myocardium and Purkinje system. Emerging evidence suggests that early corticosteroid therapy may rapidly reduce arrhythmia burden and improve ventricular function in selected patients with active myocardial inflammation. We report the case of a 34-year-old woman who presented with palpitations and syncope and was found to have BDVT secondary to acute lymphocytic myocarditis. Despite typical medical management, she had refractory ventricular arrhythmias. Prompt initiation of corticosteroids led to marked suppression of arrhythmias and rapid recovery of left ventricular ejection fraction. While current data remain limited, this case supports the potential benefit of early immunosuppressive therapy when active lymphocytic inflammation is strongly suspected.

title: Hidden and Atypical Presentations of Myocarditis in Sudden Cardiac Death: A Narrative Review.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Myocarditis is an inflammatory disease of the heart muscle, presenting from asymptomatic cases to sudden cardiac death. Its diagnosis is challenging, especially when classic cardiac symptoms are absent presents with unusual manifestations. Recognition of these unusual manifestations is essential to prevent sudden death and increase clinical awareness.

METHODS: This narrative review was conducted to summarize the evidence on myocarditis with occult and nonclassical manifestations and its role in sudden cardiac death. A systematic search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2000 and 2025. Search terms included English language, such as "myocarditis," "sudden cardiac death," "atypical presentation," "silent myocarditis," and "gastrointestinal symptoms".

RESULTS: A total of 10 studies were included and analyzed, focusing on clinical characteristics, nonclassical presentations, diagnostic findings, and outcomes. Myocarditis can be insidious and asymptomatic in young patients and increases the risk of sudden cardiac death. The diagnosis of these cases is often only possible after cardiac arrest or autopsy. In addition, myocarditis may present with nonclassical symptoms, particularly gastrointestinal symptoms, delaying diagnosis.

CONCLUSION: Myocarditis, whether asymptomatic or with nonclassical manifestations such as gastrointestinal symptoms, can be a serious health threat, especially in young people, and in some cases can cause sudden cardiac death. Evidence suggests that many of these deaths in apparently healthy individuals are due to undiagnosed myocarditis. Early recognition and attention to nonclassical symptoms are essential to prevent sudden death and improve patient management.

title: Circadian timing does not modulate human temporal contrast sensitivity.
summary: Previous studies have reported diurnal variations in color perception and luminance contrast sensitivity, suggesting modulation of visual processing by the circadian pacemaker. To clarify potential time-of-day effects, we examined whether cone-mediated temporal contrast sensitivity is modulated by circadian timing. We disentangled circadian and homeostatic influences on human visual performance using a 40-hour forced desynchrony protocol. Twelve participants (five female participants, 24.4 ± 2.9 years, range 19-30) followed a repeating 3.75-hour cycle comprising 2 hours 30 minutes of wakefulness and 1 hour 15 minutes of sleep under constant environmental conditions. Circadian period was estimated from up to 46 salivary melatonin samples per participant. During wake periods, participants repeatedly completed temporal contrast sensitivity tasks at 2 Hz and 8 Hz, using tasks that probed both luminance (L+M+S) and chromatic (L-M, S-cone-directed) modulations. We tested for circadian modulation of visual performance by comparing hierarchical cosinor models with intercept-only null models using Bayes factors. All participants showed robust melatonin rhythms (mean τ = 24.18 ± 0.39 hours). Bayesian inference provided decisive evidence against circadian variation in luminance or chromatic contrast sensitivity. Within this controlled protocol, we found no detectable near-24-hour modulation of cone-mediated temporal contrast sensitivity. Previously reported time-of-day effects may instead reflect homeostatic influences, pupil-linked changes in retinal illuminance, or mechanisms outside the cone-mediated pathways probed here. By separating circadian phase from sleep-wake-related influences, this study clarifies when circadian modulation of visual performance can and cannot be inferred.

title: Leadless Pacemakers After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Meta-analysis With Time-to-Event Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Permanent pacemaker implantation is a common complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Leadless pacemakers (LPs) may reduce lead- and pocket-related complications, but their clinical outcomes after TAVR remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety and effectiveness of LPs compared with transvenous pacemakers (TVPs).

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception to June 10, 2026. Randomized and observational studies were included. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled proportions, risk ratios (RRs), and mean differences (MDs). Reconstructed Kaplan-Meier data were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).

RESULTS: Ten studies involving 10,809 patients (1030 LP and 9779 TVP recipients) were included. The pooled procedural success rate of LP implantation was 98% (95% CI 95%-99%). Implantation success was comparable between LP and TVP (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.98-1.02). Sensitivity analysis demonstrated a shorter hospital stay with LP (MD -1.37 days, 95% CI -2.33 to -0.41) and a lower risk of heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.37, 95% CI 0.14-0.96). Overall survival did not differ between groups (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.44-1.23), although reconstructed survival curves showed late separation favoring LP. Device-related and vascular complications were comparable between LP and TVP.

CONCLUSIONS: LP implantation after TAVR demonstrates excellent procedural success and clinical outcomes comparable to TVPs. LPs may reduce hospital stay and heart failure hospitalization, supporting their use as an alternative pacing strategy in appropriately selected patients.

title: Pathogenesis, screening, and diagnosis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
summary: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a common heritable heart disease. The disease is genetically, anatomically, and clinically heterogeneous. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern but has allelic heterogeneity, incomplete penetrance, and variable expressivity. Beyond family screening, clinical evaluation for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is often prompted by identification of symptoms or detection of a heart murmur, additionally, abnormal electrocardiogram or imaging results performed for another reason can provide evidence. Evaluation should include obtaining a patient's history, a physical examination, cardiac imaging, and, often, genetic testing. Prognosis is variable; major causes of morbidity and mortality are caused by sudden cardiac death, heart failure, and atrial fibrillation with associated stroke risk. An understanding of the pathogenesis at the genetic, cellular, and individual levels helps clinicians to implement appropriate screening, recognise clinical manifestations, and improve the treatment of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The understanding of this condition is evolving, with recent advances and insights into its pathogenesis, refinement of risk stratification, and use of artificial intelligence in screening, diagnosis, and prognostication.

title: Nox4 Mediates Diastolic Function in a Genetic Model of Pitx2 Haploinsufficiency.
summary: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) commonly coexists with atrial fibrillation (AF), but shared mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we hypothesized that Pitx2, a transcription factor located near the strongest genetic locus associated with AF in humans, increases susceptibility to HFpEF-like remodeling. We also sought to understand pathways that might be central to this increased risk. Male and female Pitx2+/- mice and wild-type littermates received 3-week subcutaneous osmotic pump infusion of saline or angiotensin II (Ang II; 500 ng/kg/min). Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and catheterization, and functional capacity by exercise treadmill. RNA transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify candidate pathways. In a separate cohort, Ang II-treated mice were randomized to oral GKT136901 (30 mg/kg/day) or vehicle during infusion. After Ang II infusion, Pitx2+/- mice developed exaggerated HFpEF-like changes, including greater left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and reduced treadmill performance. RNA-seq showed enrichment of metabolic and stress-response pathways with selective upregulation of Nox4, confirmed by RT-qPCR. GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility-HFpEF interactions.

title: Bone Morphogenetic Protein-10 as a Predictor of Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Catheter Ablation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Biomarkers of atrial cardiomyopathy may improve the prediction of recurrence of atrial fibrillation (AF) after catheter ablation. Bone morphogenetic protein-10 (BMP10) is an atrial-specific cardiomyocyte protein and a potential biomarker, but evidence is limited and not comprehensively synthesized.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies to evaluate the association between circulating BMP10 concentrations with AF recurrence after catheter ablation. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were computed using a random-effects model. The primary analysis used unadjusted HRs per continuous BMP10 levels from all included studies. Secondary analyses were conducted based on the adjusted HRs of studies with continuous BMP10 and all studies, including one study that reported adjusted HRs based on quartiles.

RESULTS: Three studies were included. In the primary analysis without adjustment (n = 3), increased levels of BMP10 were significantly associated with recurrence of AF (pooled HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.13-2.07; P = 0.006), with moderate-to-high heterogeneity (I2 = 69%). The association was attenuated and non-significant in the adjusted analysis of two studies with continuous BMP10 (HR 1.46, 95% CI 0.94-2.25; I2 = 59%). However, after the inclusion of a third study with adjusted quartile-based HR, the statistical significance was re-demonstrated (HR 1.33, 95% CI 1.16-1.53; P < 0.001) with low heterogeneity (I2 = 20%).

CONCLUSION: Elevated BMP10 levels are correlated with higher risk of AF recurrence following catheter ablation. Although the results are consistent across analyses, they should be interpreted with caution due to the small number of studies and methodological heterogeneity. BMP10 needs to be confirmed as a clinically applicable biomarker by larger prospective studies.
